2   ORDER

Present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is directed against the order dated 01.12.2020 passed by Director General of Police, whereby appeal preferred by the petitioner against the order dated 26.06.2020 passed by Deputy Inspector General of Police was dismissed.

2. Petitioner is aggrieved by order dated 26.06.2020 passed by Deputy Inspector General of Police,
whereby while affirming the order of dismissal of the petitioner from service, the appeal preferred by the petitioner was dismissed, wherein challenge was made to the order dated 22.09.2019 passed by Superintendent of Police, District Guna, whereby petitioner has been dismissed from service though the charges levelled against him were not proved.

3. Short facts of the case are that the petitioner, who was appointed on the post of Constable on 17.07.2014, faced with a complaint made by one Prakash Dhakad S/o Janak Singh Dhakad alleging that he had demanded Rs.2,00,000/- from him for getting him appointed in government service,
but neither the complainant secured any appointment nor the money was returned.
4. On the basis of aforesaid complaint, preliminary enquiry was conducted.

On the basis of aforesaid preliminary enquiry, petitioner was charge-sheeted on 10.01.2019 and singular charge of demanding and receiving Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant for his appointment in the government service was made.

The departmental enquiry was initiated and the petitioner was given an opportunity to file his reply, to which, petitioner had submitted his reply and thereafter, after appointment of enquiry officer 3 WP-13923-2022 and the presenting officer, statements of the witnesses were recoded.

In all, five witnesses were examined as departmental witnesses; complainant Prakash Dhakad as PW-1, Officer, who has conducted preliminary enquiry Rajendra Singh, SDO(P) as PW-2 and Deepak Gaud as PW-3, Satish - Assistant Sub-Inspector as PW-4 and Rashmi wife of the complainant as PW-5.
5.
In his statement, complainant Prakash though admitted that he had signed the complaint, but he denied that he had given Rs.2,00,000/- to the petitioner in lieu of getting a government job.

Further, complainant had made specific averments in his statement that because of some hot conversation between him and the petitioner, in a fit of anger, he had made a complaint and at no point of time, any demand was made by the petitioner.
Further, it is stated in the petition that the petitioner was not allowed to cross-examine the said witness.

Also with regard to Rashmi (PW-5)
wife of the complainant, it has been alleged that the petitioner was not given an opportunity to cross- examine her and her evidence was taken at home without any information to the petitioner and apart from the statements of these two witnesses, there are no facts, which could be said to be against the petitioner, to involve him with the incident.

sentences.text: After recording of the evidence of all the witnesses, enquiry officer in his conclusion had found that though the factum of giving Rs.2,00,000/- to the petitioner can be said to be proved, but for what purpose the said amount was given is not proved by either of the witnesses or from the documents available on record and in the light of the aforesaid finding, the charge 4 WP-13923-2022 levelled against the petitioner was found to be partly proved and the report so prepared was forwarded to the disciplinary authority.

The disciplinary authority vide impugned order dated 22.09.2019 apart from the aforesaid report, called for the past conduct of the petitioner and found that in contrast to 16 awards, he has been punished six times and also against the petitioner, certain crimes vide Crime No.118/2019 under Section 382 of IPC at Police Station Dehat Shivpuri, another Crime No.770/2019 under Section 420 of IPC at Police Station Cantt., District Guna were registered and he was also arrested.

Thus, holding the petitioner to be having criminal antecedents, coupled with the charge partly proved against him, he found the petitioner not fit to remain in the police service and, accordingly, major penalty of his dismissal from service was passed.

7. Against the said order, petitioner preferred an appeal before the Deputy Inspector General of Police, which came to be decided vide order dated 22.06.2019, whereby appeal was dismissed and the order passed by Superintendent of Police dated 22.09.2019 was affirmed.

Against the said order,
petitioner preferred second appeal before the Director General of Police, which came to be decided vide order dated 01.12.2020, which also received the same fate as the orders passed by the two authorities thereupon and the second appeal was also dismissed.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid, present petition has been filed.

8. Shri MPS Raghuvanshi, learned Senior Counsel along with Shri Mohammad Amir, learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that in the departmental enquiry conducted against the present petitioner, charge 5 WP-13923-2022 levelled against the petitioner was found to be partly proved and in categorical terms, enquiry officer had observed that though the factum of taking of Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant is proved, but the purpose for which, it was taken, from the statements of the witnesses and evidence available on record, was not found to be proved, but even then, while concluding, the enquiry officer had made observation that the factum of taking of Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant in the name of securing a government job is proved, which is against Para 64(8) of Police Regulation, therefore, same amounts to misconduct, which though is not in consonance with the finding arrived at by the enquiry officer himself, but had not been noted by the disciplinary authority while passing the order.
9.

It was further submitted that if the disciplinary authority was not agreeing with the findings of the enquiry officer, then he was required to record its reasons as provided under Rule 15(2) of Madhya Pradesh (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1966 (in short "Rules, 1966"), but no such reasons have been recorded by the disciplinary authority, which makes the enquiry report vulnerable and there was no occasion for the disciplinary authority to take contrary view and to saddle with a major penalty of dismissal from service upon the petitioner.

It was further argued that if the disciplinary authority would have only on the basis of enquiry report awarded punishment, the punishment would have been altogether different, but the disciplinary authority had gone a step ahead on the basis of past conduct of the petitioner, to which,
he was not noticed at all and regarding which, no opportunity of hearing was available to the petitioner and as a surprise, the petitioner was saddled with the penalty of dismissal from service,
which is against the principles of natural justice.

It was submitted that on all the counts, penalty of dismissal from srvice is too excessive, even if it is assumed that petitioner has taken Rs.2,00,000/-
from the complainant.

12. Per contra, Shri M.S. Jadon, learned counsel appearing for the State, had supported the impugned orders and has contended that the enquiry officer had found proved allegations levelled against the petitioner, specially in the light of the statement of Rashmi (PW-5) wife of the complainant, who in specific words, has stated that petitioner has taken Rs.2,00,000/- from her husband for securing a government job for him, but neither job was got secured nor the money was returned back and whenever she had asked for returning of the money, the petitioner had abused her.

It was further submitted that the petitioner though was given an opportunity to cross- examine the said witness, he had given up the cross-examination upon her, which made allegations against the present petitioner of demand of money for securing government job, proved.

13. It was further submitted that not only Prakash, who had lodged a 7 WP-13923-2022 complaint against the present petitioner but his wife Rashmi (PW-5) was also one of the complainant and she,
in categorical terms, had stated that she had also signed the complaint along with PW-1 complainant; her husband and had admitted her signatures over the complaint, which is enough to presume that the complaint was genuine and not a fake one and merely on an observation made by the enquiry officer, that the purpose for which money was given to the present petitioner could not be proved, statement of Rashmi (PW-5) cannot be belied and on it's basis, it can very well be said that the money was demanded by the petitioner only for the purpose of getting the complainant a government job.
14.

It was further contended that apart from proving of the charge against the petitioner, the disciplinary authority had also found that the petitioner had criminal antecedents and two criminal cases vide Crime No.118/2019 and 770/2019 were registered against him and thus, as a cumulative effect of both the factors, petitioner was found not to be fit to remain in police service and,
accordingly, order of dismissal came to be passed, which cannot be arbitrary.
On the basis of aforesaid arguments, it was submitted that present petition deserves to be dismissed.

15. It was further contended that because the case of the petitioner is squarely covered under Para 64(8) of Police Regulations as the factum of taking of money have been proved against the petitioner when there is specific bar under the said Regulation to accept any money even as a loan from any police officer or any other person and since the petitioner admittedly had taken a sum of Devendra Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134183670/
4 Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant, the order 8 WP-13923-2022 of dismissal from service has rightly been passed.
16.

17. To analyze aforesaid controversy, this Court first deems it fit to analyze the amputation of charge made against the petitioner, which reads as under:-

The allegations against the petitioner was that he had demanded Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant Prakash Dhakad for getting his appointment on a government job, which is in total derogation of Para 64(8) of Police Regulations and amounts to misconduct.

Para 64(8) of Police Regulations reads as under:-
64. General Condition of Service .-Every candidate for an appointment in the police should be made acquainted, prior to appointment, with the general conditions of police service, which are as follows:-
xxx xxx xxxx (8)

He shall promptly discharge such debts as the Superintendent may direct and shall not without the Superintendent's per-mission, have money transactions with any other police officer, or borrow money from a resident of the district in which he is employed.

19. Para 64(8) of Police Regulations provides that every candidate for an appointment in the police service should be made acquainted, prior to appointment, with the general conditions of police service, and one of which 9 WP-13923-2022 is that he shall promptly discharge such debts as the Superintendent may direct and shall not without the Superintendent's permission have money transaction with any other police officer, or borrow money from a resident of the district, in which he is employed.

20. Herein allegation against the petitioner is not that he had borrowed some money from a third person or enter into any money transaction with police officer without permission of Superintendent of Police, but the allegation is that he had demanded some money from the complainant, who is relative of the petitioner for getting a government job.

The enquiry officer after conducting entire enquiry had found that though money transaction between the two is said to be proved, but for what purpose, the money has been taken had not been proved by the witnesses or the material available on record.

Thus, the question of borrowing of any money from the complainant does not arise, coupled with the fact that the complainant Prakash (PW-1) himself has admitted that whatever dispute was between the two, has been settled.
Thus, when the very provisions of Para 64(8) of Police Regulations are not fulfilled, then imposing penalty of dismissal from service taking resort to the said provisions could not be sustained.

sentences.text: Apart from the aforesaid observations, this Court also finds that the disciplinary authority had not disagreed with this finding of enquiry officer that the purpose of money transaction between the two had not been found to be proved, nor has given any reasoning to counter the said finding as provided in Rule 15(2) of the Rules, 1966.

Apart from the aforesaid, another glaring feature, which is seen from the very order of disciplinary authority, is 10 WP-13923-2022 that he had arrived at a conclusion from dismissal from service on the basis of certain facts, for which, no show cause notice was ever issued to the petitioner, i.e., past conduct of the petitioner having two criminal antecedents and this Court finds that no opportunity of hearing in that regard was available to the petitioner, to have controverted the said fact or would have meted out the said facts.
22.

Thus, there is no hesitation to hold that the order passed by the disciplinary authority, i.e.,
Superintendent of Police while passing the said order appears to be in total derogation of principles of natural justice, coupled with total misreading of the enquiry report.

Therefore, in the light of the aforesaid discussion, the said order does not withstand judicial scrutiny, accordingly, the same is hereby set aside, as a natural corollary, the orders of the first appellate authority as well as second appellate authority are also hereby quashed.
23. Resultantly, the respondents are directed to reinstate the petitioners, forthwith, with all backwages and other benefits attached to the post.
24. With aforesaid observations, this petition stands disposed of.
